messages.subject: determining memory usage
parts:
Dear List,

I am using stan via rstan, and wanted to know how to determine the memory usage (and how to expand memory, if necessary).   

Thanks, and regards,
Margaret Donald

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] determining memory usage
parts:
R will auto-expand memory until you don't have
any more.

If you save in RStan directly rather than writing out
to a file, then I think it'll take at least 8 bytes per
parameter (count cells in matrices, etc.) per iteration, and maybe
there's a factor of 2 in there for peak memory usage (I'm not
following exactly). And it'll take 8 bytes per data value.
Then there's some overhead for R itself, which you can
measure when R starts up and will depend on whether you're
running 32-bit or 64-bit R.

If you stream out to a CSV file, there's no per-parameter
overhead (besided a little bit used in the leapfrog steps,
maybe the equivalent of 10 iterations worth).

- Bob
